edges.description: SPACRCAN is one of the two main chondroitin-sulfate proteoglycans that build the IPM; without it the matrix scaffold is not assembled normally.
Without IMPG2 to position it, IMPG1 is no longer confined to the outer-segment matrix and accumulates abnormally in the subretinal space.
Extrapolated from the mouse, which shows reduced visual function rather than frank photoreceptor loss; the step to human photoreceptor degeneration is inferred.
The link from subretinal material to the human macular involvement is extrapolated from the mouse; the human subretinal correlate is not established.
Mislocalized IMPG1 accumulates between outer segments and RPE as subretinal lesions.
edges.limitations: Mice have no macula, so lesions are not confined to a central vitelliform focus; the phenotype is driven by mislocalized mouse IMPG1 rather than by a patient IMPG2 allele.

edges.description: Shortened rod and cone outer segments in embryonic retina.
edges.limitations: Transient knockdown in developing fish retina reports outer-segment length only and does not model the adult-onset progressive course.

nodes.description: Both IMPG2 alleles carry a null variant (nonsense, genomic deletion) or a missense variant, so photoreceptors make little or no functional SPACRCAN. The SEA-domain-deletion allele is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum in vitro rather than reaching the cell surface, and IMPG2 is a structural constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.

nodes.description: A homozygous 1.8 kb genomic deletion removing exon 9 and seven amino acids of a conserved SEA domain; the mutant protein is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum in a cell-based assay, consistent with loss of function.

nodes.description: Global Impg2 knockout in which IMPG1 fails to localize to the outer-segment matrix and instead accumulates between the outer segments and the RPE, producing subretinal lesions, microglial activation and reduced visual function; the double Impg1/Impg2 knockout is normal, showing the mislocalized IMPG1 drives the phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Proteoglycan IMPG2 Shapes the Interphotoreceptor Matrix and Modulates Vision.
evidence.snippet: mice lacking both IMPG1 and IMPG2, regardless of sex, showed normal retinal structure and function, demonstrating that the aberrant IMPG1 distribution is the main cause of the visual alterations observed in the absence of IMPG2

nodes.description: IMPG2 occupies the inner-segment side of the IPM and, with IMPG1, supplies most of its chondroitin sulfate and the cone glycocalyx. IMPG2 at the inner segment is required to position IMPG1 in the outer-segment compartment, so loss of IMPG2 disrupts the organization of the matrix.

evidence.reference_title: Proteoglycan IMPG2 Shapes the Interphotoreceptor Matrix and Modulates Vision.
evidence.snippet: In normal retina, IMPG1 and IMPG2 occupy distinct IPM compartments, represent the main source of chondroitin sulfate and are fundamental for the constitution of the cone-specific glycocalyx stained by the PNA (peanut agglutinin) lectin marker.

evidence.reference_title: Proteoglycan IMPG2 Shapes the Interphotoreceptor Matrix and Modulates Vision.

nodes.description: Macular involvement is a frequent, relatively early feature of IMPG2 RP: a 17-patient cohort found macular abnormalities in every patient, ranging from mild pigment mottling through bull's-eye maculopathy to macular chorioretinal atrophy. A maculopathy was also the presenting feature of the recessive missense patient in the founding report.

evidence.reference_title: IMPG2-associated retinitis pigmentosa displays relatively early macular involvement.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, we observed macular abnormalities in all patients, ranging from subtle mottling of the macular pigment epithelium (two patients) and a bull's eye maculopathy (seven patients) to macular chorioretinal atrophy (seven patients).
